title: Teaching, Teacher Education & Curriculum
subtitle: a graduate-level guide to the craft of teaching, how teachers are made, and how curriculum is designed, with a high-leverage practice explorer and a scored theory self-check
problem: Teacher candidates, instructional coaches and curriculum leaders talk fluently about constructivism and rigour and then run a classroom by habit: a drill that is really behaviourist, a discussion that is really coverage, a curriculum map that lists topics without evidence of learning. The theories are known; the connection from a theory to a specific move, and from a move to a design decision, is rarely made explicit.
solution: An eleven-section resource that grounds teaching in five learning traditions, names the high-leverage practices novices can rehearse, sets out culturally relevant and inclusive teaching, argues for practice-based teacher education and job-embedded development, goes discipline-deep into mathematics and science education, treats curriculum as intended, enacted, hidden and assessed with backward design at scale, and separates assessment for learning from assessment of it — with a practice explorer and a scored self-check that asks the reader to name the theory behind five classroom activities.
pedagogy: name the theory behind the move: the self-check gives immediate feedback on why an activity reflects behaviourism, cognitivism, constructivism, social constructivism or connectivism; the practice explorer shows what each move looks like in a classroom, not only what it is called; discipline sections use the field's own frameworks (NCTM, NGSS).
